ai-at-work.title: Naïve raises $28.5M to automate the grunt work of setting up and running a company
ai-at-work.excerpt: Taking vibe-coding a step further, Naïve claims its infra can automate most of the work in setting up and running a business.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Naïve just grabbed $28.5 million to automate the administrative grunt work that keeps companies running, from setup through daily operations. This matters because digital workplace teams already spend half their time on repetitive tasks that could be handled by automation, so tools that eliminate this friction directly impact productivity and headcount allocation. The real question is whether "automating business operations" becomes another shiny tool that sits unused because nobody actually configured it properly, which, ironically, requires exactly the kind of grunt work they're trying to eliminate.

ai-at-work.title: OpenAI says Apple’s own security practices undermine its trade secrets case
ai-at-work.excerpt: Newly filed court exhibits show OpenAI’s legal strategy in Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit: argue that Apple’s own security and offboarding practices — including allowing an Apple manager to access a fo
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI is essentially telling the court that Apple can't claim trade secret theft when Apple itself let a manager snoop through a departed engineer's personal iCloud account. For digital workplace pros, this is a sharp reminder that security theater means nothing if your offboarding process is sloppy and your access controls are basically suggestions. The irony is delicious: Apple lectures everyone on privacy while apparently treating employee data like it's a communal filing cabinet.

ai-at-work.title: Ex-Spotify employees raise $10M to bring the AI behind its recommendations to e-commerce
ai-at-work.excerpt: The startup's platform predicts which product a shopper wants next, learns their general taste, and fine-tunes continuously based on what they do in real time.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Some ex-Spotify engineers spun out a startup that takes recommendation algorithms from music streaming and applies them to online shopping, raising 10 million dollars to do it. This matters to digital workplace pros because recommendation engines are becoming table stakes for employee experience platforms, knowledge management systems, and internal marketplaces where personalization actually drives adoption. Here's the thing though: most companies still can't get their org charts right in their directory, so watching startups chase the next shiny algorithmic problem while basic workplace data hygiene remains a mess is pretty rich.

ai-at-work.title: Exclusive: Mirendil inks $100M+ Google Cloud deal to scale self-improving AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Mirendil has signed a $100 million-plus Google Cloud partnership to expand its compute infrastructure, powering research into self-improving AI systems designed to accelerate scientific discovery and
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Mirendil just locked in a $100 million Google Cloud deal to beef up its computing power for self-improving AI research. This matters because if these systems actually deliver on faster scientific breakthroughs, they could reshape how we build workplace collaboration tools, knowledge management systems, and automation workflows in the next few years. That said, I've watched enough AI announcements to know the difference between lab breakthroughs and what actually lands on your employees' desks, so let's check back in 18 months when we see what actually ships.

tools-tech.title: You can use 70+ Adobe tools without leaving ChatGPT now - here's how
tools-tech.excerpt: Adobe's new plugin works both in Work and Codex, and is available today in ChatGPT.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Adobe just released a ChatGPT plugin that lets you access over 70 Adobe tools directly from within ChatGPT without switching applications. For digital workplace folks, this is significant because it reduces friction in creative workflows and potentially shifts where people do their actual work (hint: increasingly, it's inside AI chatbots now). Look, I've watched enough "integrated" tools promise to simplify life only to create more confusion, so let's see if this actually sticks or becomes another forgotten plugin gathering dust in someone's toolbar.

tools-tech.title: Cloudflare wants to provide the operating system for the AI-first enterprise
tools-tech.excerpt: Traditional operating systems (OS) were built to manage hardware, files, apps, and users on a device, but Cloudflare says the agentic AI era requires a whole new format. The company this week announce
tools-tech.dwp_take: Cloudflare just launched an open source, browser-based operating system designed to connect AI agents, enterprise data, internal systems, and workflows into one unified workspace instead of managing individual devices the old way. For digital workplace teams, this matters because it signals the shift from device-centric to workflow-centric architecture, which means your entire approach to security, access, and user experience needs rethinking now, not later. Honestly, if this actually works as advertised, it could finally answer the question "where does the AI agent sit in our tech stack" that's been keeping workplace leaders up at night, though I'll believe the "open source" promise when I see how long that lasts.

tools-tech.title: Granola lawsuit raises concerns over AI note-taking app privacy
tools-tech.excerpt: AI note-taking app maker Granola is accused of violating privacy laws by developing software that can record conversations without all participants’ consent, according to a lawsuit filed July 30 in a
tools-tech.dwp_take: Granola, an AI note-taking app, is being sued for allegedly recording conversations without everyone's consent, joining a similar lawsuit against competitor Otter.ai. This matters because digital workplace professionals are increasingly deploying these tools for meeting capture and knowledge management, but legal liability over consent and recording laws could kill adoption overnight. Turns out "we're recording this for your safety" doesn't actually work as a legal defense in most states, which explains why both companies are now having a very expensive learning moment.

tools-tech.title: Enterprise passkey security under threat from malware
tools-tech.excerpt: Given the widespread enterprise adoption of passkeys to replace passwords, a Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 report disclosing ways attackers are getting around passkey protections is concerning, analysts
tools-tech.dwp_take: Palo Alto Networks found that attackers can bypass passkey protections, but only after they've already compromised your system. This matters because if your organization bet the farm on passkeys as your security silver bullet, you're learning the hard way that they're just one layer, not a firewall. The real takeaway: passkeys are great, but pretending they're magic and then ignoring basic endpoint security is how you end up explaining things to your CISO.

digital-culture.title: What Fauci’s diary leak should remind employees about privacy at work
digital-culture.excerpt: Last month, Anthony Fauci was subpoenaed by Republican Senator Rand Paul regarding the origins of COVID-19 and his broader pandemic policy oversight. Paul has disagreed publicly over the origins of th
digital-culture.dwp_take: Someone leaked Fauci's private diary entries during a high-profile political dispute, raising serious questions about what counts as "private" even for public figures. For digital workplace folks, this is a wake-up call that personal notes, emails, and digital communications can become evidence or public fodder faster than you'd think, regardless of your job title. The real lesson here isn't "don't write honest things down" but rather "assume your digital paper trail could end up on the front page someday, so write accordingly."

digital-culture.title: It’s time to open the black box of AI-driven employment decisions
digital-culture.excerpt: Following my own experience fighting pregnancy discrimination, I’ve come to think of employment discrimination as a black box. Workers who are denied promotions, passed over for opportunities, or sele
digital-culture.dwp_take: Employers are increasingly using AI to make hiring and firing decisions without transparency, leaving workers in the dark about why they're promoted, passed over, or laid off. This matters hugely to digital workplace professionals because we're often the ones implementing these systems, and we need to understand the legal and ethical landmines we're walking through. Here's the uncomfortable truth: if you can't explain why your AI made a decision, you're probably building a discrimination machine wrapped in algorithms.

digital-culture.title: Why Normal People Aren’t Using AI Agents
digital-culture.excerpt: The tech industry is realizing it needs to build agents based on what regular consumers want, not just what its AI models can do.
digital-culture.dwp_take: The tech industry finally figured out that AI agents designed for what engineers think is cool don't actually solve problems people care about. This matters to digital workplace pros because your leadership is about to ask you to implement AI solutions that nobody asked for, and you'll need to push back with user research instead of just saying yes. The real work isn't making AI do more things, it's making it do the three things your users actually need without breaking their workflow in the process.

industry-news.title: ChatGPT Atlas Shuts Down Aug. 9: What Users Must Save Before Migrating
industry-news.excerpt: ChatGPT Atlas is scheduled to stop working Aug. 9, 2026. Users should export browser data, verify account access, and test replacement workflows before uninstalling it. The post ChatGPT Atlas Shuts Do
industry-news.dwp_take: ChatGPT Atlas is getting shut down on August 9, 2026, and users need to export their data and test new workflows before it disappears. This matters because organizations that built processes around this tool now face a migration scramble, which is exactly the kind of vendor lock-in problem that keeps IT leaders up at night. Here's the real lesson: stop treating AI tools like permanent infrastructure and start treating them like the beta products they actually are.

industry-news.excerpt: Google's August Android 17 update fixes Pixel 10 gaming, GPU, and touchscreen issues while bringing the latest security patch to supported Pixel devices. The post Google Rolls Out August Android 17 Up
industry-news.dwp_take: Google pushed out an August Android 17 update that squashes gaming, GPU, and touchscreen bugs on Pixel 10 devices while bundling in the latest security patches. For digital workplace folks managing Pixel devices across their organizations, this matters because stability fixes directly reduce support tickets and keep mobile workers productive instead of frustrated. Here's the real talk: if your team is running Pixels, you're getting a free stability bump that actually works, which is refreshing compared to the usual "update that creates two new problems" cycle we've all lived through.

industry-news.title: Samsung: New Galaxy Foldables Beat Previous Preorder Record by 30%
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 leads record foldable preorders in the US and South Korea as more buyers move from Flip models to the larger Fold lineup before launch. The post Samsung: New Galaxy Foldables
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold8 foldable phones are crushing preorder records, up 30 percent from the last generation, with more customers choosing the larger Fold over the Flip model. This matters to digital workplace folks because foldables are finally becoming real productivity devices instead of novelties, which means your organization needs to think about how these screens will change work habits and security protocols. Honestly, if people are willing to pay that much for a phone that folds, maybe they're finally ready to actually use it for something beyond Instagram.
